claim: TubeArchivist supports a YouTube cookie that, once imported, turns Watch Later and Liked Videos into regular subscribable/downloadable playlists; validity is checked by whether yt-dlp can access the private Liked Videos playlist, and the cookie is stored in Redis and shared across all users (one cookie per instance).
quote: A cookie is considered as valid if yt-dlp is able to access your private Liked Videos playlist... There is only one cookie per Tube Archivist instance, and this will be shared between all users.

claim: TubeArchivist warns that YouTube has a detection mechanism that invalidates cookies used outside a browser, and that the cookie contains the Google account access token and must be treated like a password.
quote: It appears that YT has some detection mechanism that will invalidate your cookie if it's being used outside of a browser... Treat that data with utmost care, as you would any other password or credential.

claim: PinchFlat takes a cookies.txt at /config/extras/cookies.txt with a per-source Cookie Behaviour setting (Disabled / When Needed / All Operations), and its wiki warns yt-dlp no longer recommends YouTube cookies because they can trigger IP bans.
quote: yt-dlp no longer recommends using YouTube cookies since they can cause YouTube to issue IP bans.

claim: TubeSync (v0.10+) accepts a Netscape-format cookies file to authenticate to YouTube; users have used it to pull their Liked Videos playlist by exporting youtube.com cookies, with the caveat that this identifies the Google account as using TubeSync and is entirely at the user's own risk.
quote: Using cookies exported from your browser that is authenticated to YouTube identifies your Google account as using TubeSync, which may result in potential account impacts and is entirely at your own risk.

claim: yt-dlp recommends extracting cookies via --cookies-from-browser or a browser extension, that the exported file contains cookies for ALL sites, and that cookies should be exported from a fresh browser session within the past 30 minutes.
quote: the cookies need to be exported from a fresh browser session... within the past 30 minutes... this method exports your browser's cookies for ALL sites... so take care in not letting this text file fall into the wrong hands.

claim: MeTube accepts cookies either via an Upload Cookies button in the web UI Advanced Options (showing an active cookie indicator) or via the YTDL_OPTIONS environment variable as a JSON object with a cookiefile key, which can target a private playlist or Liked Videos.
quote: YTDL_OPTIONS: Additional options to pass to youtube-dl, in JSON format... keys are the yt-dlp API option names, which roughly correspond to command-line flags with dashes replaced by underscores.

claim: In 2026 Chrome 127+ app-bound encryption binds cookie decryption keys to the Chrome binary, breaking external extraction, while Firefox stores cookies in a plain SQLite database making it the only reliably working source; yt-dlp OAuth2 for YouTube has been deprecated, and exported cookies expire in roughly two weeks.
quote: Firefox doesn't encrypt cookies. Firefox stores cookies in a plain SQLite database... Chrome 127+ ... app-bound encryption that binds decryption keys to the Chrome binary itself... yt-dlp OAuth2 — YouTube deprecated this method.

claim: ytdl-sub can download from a YouTube playlist (including Watch Later / Liked Videos via a cookiefile in ytdl_options) but keeping the local archive in sync by removing items no longer in the source playlist is an open feature request rather than built-in behavior.
quote: Sync Capability: Automatically remove items that are not in a playlist anymore
